data.context: How We Used Machine Learning to to Pinpoint the Magecart Crime Syndicate.

evidence.quote: Used Machine Learning to to Pinpoint the Magecart Crime Syndicate

data.context: In this blog, we'll investigate what happened during the breach of British Airways customer data made public on September 6, which spanned a total of 15 days according to public reporting.

evidence.quote: breach of British Airways customer data

data.context: Magecart uses a digital variety of these devices.

evidence.quote: Magecart uses a digital variety of these devices.

data.context: Magecart injects scripts designed to steal sensitive data that consumers enter into online payment forms on e-commerce websites directly or through compromised third-party suppliers used by these sites.

evidence.quote: Magecart injects scripts designed to steal sensitive data

data.context: Based on recent evidence, Magecart has now set their sights on British Airways, the largest airline in the UK.

evidence.quote: has now set their sights on British Airways

data.context: Finding the Breach of British Airways Our first step in linking Magecart to the attack on British Airways was simply going through our Magecart detection hits.

evidence.quote: linking Magecart to the attack on British Airways

data.context: Seeing instances of Magecart is so common for us that we get at least hourly alerts for websites getting compromised with their skimmer-code.

evidence.quote: Seeing instances of Magecart is so common for us that we get at least hourly alerts for websites getting compromised with their skimmer-code.

data.context: For this research, we decided to focus our efforts by identifying individual scripts on the British Airways website and examining their appearance over time - we would verify all the unique scripts on the website and only look at them again if their appearance changed in our crawling.

evidence.quote: identifying individual scripts on the British Airways website

data.context: Opening up the crawl, we saw this script was a modified version of the Modernizr JavaScript library, version 2.6.2 to be precise.

evidence.quote: was a modified version of the Modernizr JavaScript library, version 2.6.2 to be precise.

data.context: Fig-2 The suspicious script tag added by Magecart We found more evidence in the server headers sent by the British Airways server.

evidence.quote: The suspicious script tag added by Magecart

data.context: The servers send a 'Last-Modified' header, which indicates the last time a piece of static content was modified.

evidence.quote: which indicates the last time a piece of static content was modified.

data.context: The clean version of the Modernizr script had a timestamp from December 2012: Fig-3 Clean version of the compromised script

evidence.quote: had a timestamp

data.context: We can see on the modified, malicious version of Modernizr the timestamp matches closely to the timestamp given by British Airways as the beginning of people getting victimized: Fig-4 Timestamp of when the skimming began Here is a cleaned up version of the script, only 22 lines of JavaScript: Fig-5 Only 22 lines of script victimized 380,000 people

evidence.quote: We can see on the modified, malicious version of Modernizr the timestamp matches closely to the timestamp given by British Airways as the beginning of people getting victimized

data.context: This means that once a user hits the button to submit their payment on the compromised British Airways site, the information from the payment form is extracted along with their name and sent to the attacker's server.

evidence.quote: the information from the payment form is extracted

data.context: This attack is a simple but highly targeted approach compared to what we've seen in the past with the Magecart skimmer which grabbed forms indiscriminately.

evidence.quote: Magecart skimmer

data.context: This particular skimmer is very much attuned to how British Airway's payment page is set up, which tells us that the attackers carefully considered how to target this site instead of blindly injecting the regular Magecart skimmer.

evidence.quote: instead of blindly injecting the regular Magecart skimmer.

data.context: What is interesting to note from the certificate the Magecart actors used is that it was issued on August 15th, which indicates they likely had access to the British Airways site before the reported start date of the attack on August 21st - possibly long before.

evidence.quote: which indicates they likely had access to the British Airways site before the reported start date of the attack on August 21st - possibly long before

data.context: Without visibility into its Internet-facing web assets, British Airways were not able to detect this compromise before it was too late.

evidence.quote: visibility into its Internet-facing web assets

data.context: We found the skimmer on the webpage for British Airways, but how does that translate to mobile?

evidence.quote: We found the skimmer on the webpage

data.context: To figure this out we'll look at the British Airways Android application:

evidence.quote: British Airways Android application

data.context: Fig-7 British Airways mobile application Often, when developers build a mobile app, they make an empty shell and load content from elsewhere.

evidence.quote: they make an empty shell

data.context: In the case of British Airways, a portion of the app is native but the majority of its functionality loads from web pages from the official British Airways website.

evidence.quote: from the official British Airways website

data.context: The mobile app uses a set of different hosts to communicate back to the British Airways servers: www.britishairways.com (The main website) api4-prl.baplc.com (An API endpoint from British Airways)

evidence.quote: The mobile app uses a set of different hosts

data.context: api4.baplc.com (Another API endpoint from British Airways)

object.name: Another API endpoint from British Airways

evidence.quote: Another API endpoint from British Airways

data.context: The idea is that for quick data updates on its UI the app uses the API endpoints, but for searching, booking, and managing flights the app loads a mobile version of the main website.

evidence.quote: the app uses the API endpoints

data.context: Fig-8 Magecart-compromised mobile web page Now, if we look at the source of this webpage we find something interesting - the page is built with the same CSS and JavaScript components as the real website, meaning design and functionality-wise, it's a total match.

evidence.quote: the same CSS and JavaScript components as the real website

data.context: Conclusions As we've seen in this attack, Magecart set up custom, targeted infrastructure to blend in with the British Airways website specifically and avoid detection for as long as possible.

evidence.quote: Magecart set up custom, targeted infrastructure to blend in with the British Airways website specifically

data.context: While we can never know how much reach the attackers had on the British Airways servers, the fact that they were able to modify a resource for the site tells us the access was substantial, and the fact they likely had access long before the attack even started is a stark reminder about the vulnerability of web-facing assets RiskIQ has been warning the market about Magecart attacks like this since 2015 and will continue to follow and report on the group as it evolves.

evidence.quote: While we can never know how much reach the attackers had on the British Airways servers

data.context: While the Magecart attack against British Airways wasn't a compromise of a third-party supplier like the attack on Ticketmaster, it does raise the question of payment form security.

evidence.quote: While the Magecart attack against British Airways wasn't a compromise of a third-party supplier like the attack on Ticketmaster, it does raise the question of payment form security.

data.context: Magecart is an active threat that operates at a scale and breadth that rivals - or possibly surpasses - the recent compromises of point-of-sale systems of retail giants such as Home Depot and Target.

evidence.quote: Magecart is an active threat that operates at a scale and breadth that rivals - or possibly surpasses - the recent compromises of point-of-sale systems

data.context: Over time, they've optimized their tactics culminating in successful breaches of third-party providers such as Inbenta resulting in the theft of Ticketmaster customer data.

evidence.quote: resulting in the theft of Ticketmaster customer data.

data.context: We're now seeing them target specific brands, crafting their attacks to match the functionality of specific sites, which we saw in the breach of British Airways.

evidence.quote: We're now seeing them target specific brands

data.context: There will be more Magecart attacks, and RiskIQ will be tracking them and keeping the cybersecurity industry aware of our research.

evidence.quote: There will be more Magecart attacks
